# Legal review — data inventory & open questions

<!-- LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED -->

**This document is a factual audit of the codebase, not legal advice.** It was generated by
reading the actual code (schema, services, adapters, env config) as of 2026-07-21, and every claim
below is traceable to a specific file. It is the input a lawyer needs to review `/privacy` and
`/terms` — those two pages are drafted from this document and are themselves marked DRAFT /
NOT REVIEWED. Nothing here should be treated as a final compliance statement.

---

## 1. What personal data is stored

### Account (Better Auth tables — `packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma`)

| Table | Columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `user` (model `User`, lines 99–122) | `id`, `name`, `email` (unique), `tagline`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `emailVerified`, `image`, `timezone` (default `"UTC"`), `timezoneSetManually` | `image` is the Google avatar URL when signed in via Google. `tagline` is user-set free text on the profile. |
| `session` (lines 134–148) | `id`, `expiresAt`, `token`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `ipAddress`, `userAgent`, `userId` | Better Auth populates `ipAddress`/`userAgent` per login session automatically. **This is IP address storage — must be disclosed.** |
| `account` (lines 150–168) | `id`, `accountId`, `providerId`, `userId`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `idToken`, `accessTokenExpiresAt`, `refreshTokenExpiresAt`, `scope`, `password` (hash, for email/password accounts) | One row per sign-in method (email/password or Google). Google's `accessToken`/`refreshToken`/`idToken` are stored here when present. |
| `verification` (lines 170–180) | `id`, `identifier`, `value`, `expiresAt` | Password-reset / email-verification tokens, keyed by email (`identifier`). |

`User.timezone` — captured client-side via `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`
(`apps/web/src/features/home/api/useHomeQuery.ts:10`, `apps/web/src/features/progress/api/useProgressQuery.ts:10`,
`apps/web/src/features/profile/components/TimezoneRow.tsx:34`) and sent as an `X-Timezone` header
on every Home/Progress request, or set explicitly via `PATCH /me/timezone`
(`apps/api/src/me/me.service.ts:37-46`). Used only to compute the user's local day for streaks and
daily story eligibility (`apps/api/src/home/home.service.ts`, `apps/api/src/progress/progress.service.ts`).

### Learning data (`packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma`)

- **`UserWord`** (lines 301–336): `senseId` (which word), `level`, FSRS state (`stability`,
  `difficulty`, `dueAt`, `reps`, `lapses`, `lastReviewedAt`), and **personal free text**:
  `customTranslation`, `sourceSentence`, `sourceType`, `note`. `sourceSentence` is explicitly
  documented in-schema as user-pasted context — **it can contain anything the user was reading,
  including names, personal details, or sensitive text from their own life.** `statsByMode` is a
  derived JSON cache, no new data.
- **`Attempt`** (lines 338–357): per-drill-question history — `taskType`, `result`,
  `responseTimeMs`, `rating`, `answeredAt`. Behavioral/performance data.
- **`DrillSession`** (lines 362–378): session metadata and a frozen `plan` (JSON) of the questions
  asked, including correct answers server-side.
- **`UserStreak`** (lines 124–132): `current`, `longest`, `freezesBanked`, `lastLearningDay`.

### Generated content

- **`Story`** (lines 402–425): `title`, `blurb`, `paragraphs`, `translation`, `newWords`,
  `glossary`, plus `coverImageKey` — an R2 object key for a generated cover image. Stories are
  generated **from that specific user's vocabulary** (see §2, Groq/Ollama).
- Cover images live in Cloudflare R2 and are served from a **public, unauthenticated URL**
  (`packages/images/src/derive-url.ts:3-8` — `${R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/${coverImageKey}`, no
  signing). Anyone with the URL can view the image; the key (`stories/{storyId}.ext`) does not
  contain the username or email, but this is security-by-obscurity, not access control. **Flagged
  as an open question below.**
- **`Task`** (lines 382–396): AI-drafted drill payloads, tied to a user and a word.

### Session cookies

First-party, essential. Better Auth issues the `session` token described above; README
(`README.md:98-102`) confirms Caddy serves web and `/api` on one domain in production, so the
cookie is first-party. **No Caddy config file exists in this repository** — its actual
cookie/session-header behavior in production could not be verified from code alone (see open
questions).

### Server logs

There is **no centralized logging middleware, no request logger, and no error-tracking SDK**
anywhere in `apps/api` or `apps/worker` (`apps/api/src/main.ts` registers CORS only, no logging
interceptor). Logging is ad hoc `console.log`/`console.error` inside individual services and AI/
image adapters (e.g. `packages/ai/src/adapters/groq.adapter.ts:33,51,55,58`,
`packages/images/src/gemini.client.ts:11,73,76`, `packages/images/src/image.service.ts:29,40,43`).
These log: job type, model name, character/byte counts, and truncated prompt/summary previews
(first 80–300 characters) — **not** raw user vocabulary lists, emails, or IPs, as far as the code
shows. IP address and user agent are **not logged to console**, but they are persisted in the
`session` table (see above) via Better Auth itself, not application logging code.

Whatever the production host (VPS) or Caddy does with access logs is **outside this repo** and
unverified — flagged below.

## 2. Where data goes (third parties)

Every credential/endpoint below is enumerated from `.env.example` (the full list of external
integrations this codebase supports) cross-checked against the code that uses each key.

| Provider | Purpose | What is sent | Leaves user's region? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Groq** (`packages/ai/src/adapters/groq.adapter.ts`) | Generates the SANITY_SENTENCE check and the daily STORY draft | The prompt built by `buildPrompt()` (`packages/ai/src/adapters/prompts.ts`), which embeds `job.allowedWords` — **the user's own vocabulary allowlist, as display lemmas** (`packages/shared/src/ai.ts:26-27`), plus a target word count. No email, name, or account identifiers are sent — only vocabulary words and their part-of-speech/level state indirectly via which words were chosen upstream. | Yes — Groq is a third-party US-based inference API (`groq-sdk`, `api.groq.com`). |
| **Google Gemini** (`packages/images/src/gemini.client.ts`) | Generates the story's cover image | A text prompt built by `buildCoverPrompt()`/`buildSubject()` (`packages/images/src/image.service.ts:31-33`) from the story's **English summary/translation** — derived content, not raw personal data, but derived from that user's vocabulary/story. Sent to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`. | Yes — Google Cloud endpoint, region not pinned in code. |
| **Cloudflare Workers AI** (`packages/images/src/cloudflare.client.ts`) | Alternate cover-image provider, selected via `IMAGE_PROVIDER=cloudflare` (default is `gemini`, `packages/images/src/provider.ts:10`) | Same story-summary-derived prompt as Gemini above. Only one provider is active at a time (`packages/images/src/image.service.ts:10-13`). | Cloudflare's global network; region depends on account config. |
| **Cloudflare R2** (`packages/images/src/r2.client.ts`) | Stores generated cover images | The generated image bytes only (no text/user data). Bucket is account-scoped (`R2_ACCOUNT_ID`), region `auto`. Served publicly via `R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (see §1). | Cloudflare's network; specific region not pinned in code. |
| **Ollama** (`packages/ai/src/adapters/ollama.adapter.ts`) | Fallback/offline brain for SANITY_SENTENCE and STORY generation, run from the overnight worker batch | Same `allowedWords` prompt as Groq. **Runs locally on the VPS** (`DEFAULT_BASE_URL = 'http://localhost:11434'`, comment at lines 16-22 confirms this is deliberately the "local, unmetered brain"). | **No** — this is a genuine privacy advantage worth stating plainly in the privacy policy: when Ollama is used, vocabulary data does not leave the server at all. |
| **Google OAuth** (`apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts:42-47`) | "Sign in with Google" | Standard OAuth profile exchange (name, email, avatar) handled by Better Auth; tokens stored in the `account` table (§1). | Yes, to Google, as part of the OAuth handshake itself. |
| **Email delivery** (`apps/api/src/lib/email/email-sender.ts`) | Password reset and email-verification links | **No third-party email provider is wired up.** `emailSender` is a hardcoded `ConsoleEmailSender` that only `console.log`s the message (lines 11-17) — nothing is actually sent over the network today. `requireEmailVerification: false` (`apps/api/src/lib/auth.ts:24`), so verification is not enforced. **This must be resolved before any real user's password-reset flow works, and the eventual real provider must be added to the privacy policy's third-party table.** |
| **Hosting (VPS) / CDN** | Runs the app | Confirmed by README only (`README.md:70,100`: "not the VPS", "Caddy in prod"); no specific host name, provider, or region appears anywhere in the repository. | Unknown — flagged below. |
| **Error tracking / analytics** | — | **None found.** No Sentry, PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude, Google Analytics, or any similar SDK/config anywhere in the repo (checked `package.json` dependencies and grepped the whole tree for common SDK names/init calls). This is worth stating explicitly and positively in the privacy policy rather than leaving it ambiguous. |

## 3. Data subject rights — what's actually built

- **Export**: `GET /me/export` (`apps/api/src/me/me.controller.ts:46-61`,
  `apps/api/src/me/me.service.ts:48-71`) returns CSV or JSON of `UserWord` rows joined to the
  dictionary: word, part of speech, translation, level, FSRS stats, and dates.
  **It does NOT include `note`, `sourceSentence`, or `sourceType`** — the free-text personal
  fields flagged in §1 as the most sensitive data category are silently excluded from export.
  This is a real gap between what a GDPR access/portability right would expect and what the
  endpoint currently returns. Flagging for engineering + legal, not fixing as part of this task.
- **Deletion**: `DELETE /me` (`apps/api/src/me/me.controller.ts:63-67`,
  `apps/api/src/me/me.service.ts:73-90`) requires typing the account email to confirm, then:
  explicitly deletes each story's R2 cover image (`this.images.deleteStoryCover`), deletes
  `Verification` rows by email (not covered by any FK cascade), then deletes the `User` row —
  which cascades (`onDelete: Cascade` in the schema) through `Session`, `Account`, `UserWord`
  (→ `Attempt`), `Task`, `Story`, `DrillSession` (→ `Attempt`), and `UserStreak`. This is a real,
  complete deletion path, not a soft-delete.
- **Correction**: name is editable in-app (`InlineEditableName`); there is no UI to edit
  `customTranslation`/`note`/`sourceSentence` after adding a word, and no way to correct the
  `email` itself. Flag for lawyer/product: does "correction" require more than this?
- **Objection**: no explicit mechanism beyond deletion exists (e.g. no per-feature opt-out of AI
  story generation). Flag.

## 4. Open questions for the lawyer (do not answer these — list only)

1. **Governing jurisdiction & operator identity.** No company name, legal entity, or business
   address appears anywhere in the repository (checked `package.json`, `README.md`). The only
   contact point in the entire codebase is `feedback@wortgarten.app`
   (`apps/web/src/features/profile/ProfilePage.tsx:103`). Who is the operator, and under which
   country/state's law does the service operate?
2. **GDPR applicability.** This is a German-vocabulary app, so EU users are likely. If GDPR
   applies: what is the legal basis for each processing purpose (contract necessity for core
   learning data, legitimate interest vs. consent for AI story generation, etc.)? What data-transfer
   mechanism (SCCs or otherwise) covers sending vocabulary data to Groq (US) and Gemini (US)? Is a
   DPA needed with Groq, Google, and Cloudflare, and do any already have one in place?
3. **Minimum age.** No minimum age is enforced or stated anywhere in the signup flow
   (`apps/web/src/features/auth/SignupPage.tsx`) or the schema. A language-learning app plausibly
   attracts minors. What should the stated minimum age be, and does that trigger COPPA (US) or
   GDPR-K / equivalent "information society services offered to children" consent-age rules (EU)?
4. **CC BY-SA share-alike.** The dictionary is Wiktionary-derived content licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 /
   GFDL (attributed already on `/about`, `apps/web/src/features/about/AboutPage.tsx:53-58`). What
   does share-alike imply for: (a) the Terms' IP/ownership claims over "the service," and (b) any
   future paid tier built on top of that dictionary? Flagging per the task brief — not resolving.
5. **Retention periods.** No explicit retention/expiry policy exists in code for any table (no TTL
   jobs, no automatic purge of old `Attempt`/`DrillSession`/`Session` rows found). What should be
   retained, for how long, and should stale data (e.g. expired `Session`/`Verification` rows) be
   actively purged rather than left to accumulate?
6. **Cover-image access control.** Generated cover images are served from a public, unsigned R2 URL
   (§1). Is unauthenticated-but-unguessable access acceptable, or should these be access-controlled
   /signed URLs given they're "derived from that user's vocabulary" content?
7. **Production email provider.** None is configured (§2) — password reset currently only logs to
   the server console in development and does not send real email anywhere. This blocks real
   password-reset functionality today, independent of the privacy policy, and whichever provider is
   eventually chosen (Resend/Postmark/SES/SMTP) needs to be added to the privacy policy and
   evaluated for a DPA.
8. **Caddy / hosting configuration.** No Caddyfile or infrastructure-as-code is checked into this
   repository, so the production reverse-proxy's access-log retention, header handling, and TLS
   config could not be audited from code. Needs a look at the actual VPS config before the privacy
   policy's "cookies/technical data" section can be called complete.

## Traceability note

Every provider, table, and column named in the drafted `/privacy` and `/terms` pages
(`apps/web/src/legal/privacy.md`, `apps/web/src/legal/terms.md`) is drawn only from this document.
If a future code change adds, removes, or repurposes a data field or third-party integration, this
file and both legal pages need a corresponding update — they will otherwise silently drift out of
sync with what the app actually does, which is the exact failure mode this task was designed to
avoid.
